items.prompt: A black pawn stands on e6. Can the white rook go to d8 in one move? Predict, then check.

claims.statement: The rook slides from d4 to d8: d5, d6 and d7 are empty.

hints: Which squares lie between the rook and d8?
Is the pawn on e6 on the rook's file?
items.explain: The pawn on e6 is not on the d-file, so it blocks nothing. d5, d6 and d7 are empty and the rook reaches d8.

items.prompt: A white pawn stands on d6. Can the white rook go to d6 in one move? Predict, then check.

claims.statement: The rook cannot land on d6: its own pawn stands there.
The rook can still reach d5.

hints: Can a piece land on a square holding its own piece?
items.explain: A piece can never land on a square held by its own piece. The rook can slide as far as d5 and stops there.

items.prompt: The white rook is on a4 and a black pawn stands on e4. Can the rook go to e4 in one move? Predict, then check.

claims.statement: The rook can capture the pawn on e4: b4, c4 and d4 are empty.

hints: Count the squares between a4 and e4.
An enemy piece at the end of the line can be taken.
items.explain: b4, c4 and d4 are empty and the pawn on e4 is an enemy piece, so the rook takes it and stops there.

items.prompt: The white rook is on a4 and a black pawn stands on e4. Can the rook go to h4 in one move? Predict, then check.

claims.statement: The rook cannot get from a4 to h4: the pawn on e4 is in the way.
It can capture the pawn on e4.

hints: Is anything on the rank between a4 and h4?
What happens to squares behind a piece the rook captures?
items.explain: The pawn on e4 stops the rook. It can take the pawn but cannot pass it, so f4, g4 and h4 are out of reach in one move.

items.prompt: Can the white rook go to f6 in one move? Predict, then check.

claims.statement: The rook cannot get from d4 to f6: f6 is on neither its rank nor its file.

hints: Is f6 on the rank or the file of d4?
items.explain: f6 is not on the d-file or on the fourth rank. A rook never moves diagonally, so it would need two moves.

items.prompt: Can the white bishop go to d5 in one move? Predict, then check.

claims.statement: The bishop cannot move straight forward to d5.
It can go diagonally to e5.

hints: Is d5 on a diagonal of d4?
Which colour is d4, and which is d5?
items.explain: d5 is straight ahead, not on a diagonal. It is also a square of the other colour than d4, which a bishop can never reach.

items.prompt: A black pawn stands on d6. Can the white bishop go to g7 in one move? Predict, then check.

claims.statement: The bishop slides from d4 to g7: e5 and f6 are empty.

hints: Which squares lie between d4 and g7?
Is the pawn on d6 on that diagonal?
items.explain: The pawn on d6 is not on the diagonal d4-g7, so it blocks nothing. e5 and f6 are empty.

items.prompt: A black pawn stands on f6. Can the white bishop go to g7 in one move? Predict, then check.

claims.statement: The bishop cannot get from d4 to g7: the pawn on f6 is in the way.
It can capture the pawn on f6.

hints: Is anything on the diagonal between d4 and g7?
What can the bishop do with an enemy piece in its way?
items.explain: The pawn on f6 is on the diagonal. The bishop can take it, but cannot pass it to reach g7.

items.prompt: Black pawns stand on f6 and d6. Can the white bishop go to f6 in one move? Predict, then check.

claims.statement: The bishop can capture the pawn on f6.

hints: Is the pawn on d6 on the diagonal from d4 to f6?
What happens to a pawn that stands off the bishop's diagonal?
items.explain: The pawn on d6 is not on the diagonal d4-f6, so nothing changes; the bishop still takes on f6.
